title: Put the food shield back over the salad bar, its front lip 18-30 cm past the food
instruction: Put the portable food shield back in service over the salad bar: standing on its two end panels, centred along the row of pans, with its front lip (the customers' side, by the tray slide) 18 to 30 cm (45 to 75 mm at this 1:4 scale) beyond the customers' edge of the food pans. Do not rest it on the pans.
context: Food preparation workers and dining room and cafeteria attendants set up and break down self-service salad bars and buffets. The US FDA Food Code (3-306.11) requires food on display to be protected by counter, service-line or salad-bar food guards (sneeze guards), display cases or other effective means. A portable food shield protects the food only if its glass and front lip stand between the customers' faces and the food: the lip must reach out past the customers' edge of the pans, but pushed too far, customers can no longer reach the back of the pans under it. Staff pull the shield back to refill or wipe the pans and must set it back: square, centred along the bar, standing on its own end panels, not on the pans or the food. The 18 to 30 cm band is this task's stated rule, not a figure quoted from a code. The bar is built at 1:4.
setup: Bimanual YAM station, built at 1:4; the table top is the salad bar's counter and the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases (toward the customers' side of the bar), y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. (1-5) Five 1/3-size food pans, fixed, in a row along y: each a stainless steel pan 81 mm deep (x) by 44 mm wide (y) and 22 mm tall (a solid block here), with a 3 mm coloured card standing for the food on top, inset 2 mm from its rim, so the food's top is 25 mm above the counter. They stand side by side 2 mm apart (centres at y +9.2, +4.6, 0, -4.6 and -9.2 cm) from x 25.9 to 34.0 cm; the row runs from y -11.4 to +11.4 cm. From left (+y) to right the food is lettuce (green), tomato (red), cucumber (pale green), sweetcorn (yellow) and croutons (tan). Their customer-side edge is the line x 34.0 cm. (6) Tray slide: a fixed stainless rail 10 mm (x) by 320 mm (y) and 10 mm tall, from x 43.4 to 44.4 cm, centred on y 0, on the customers' side 94 mm past the pans. (7) Portable food shield, loose, one rigid body, 0.25 kg: a clear acrylic top glass 80 mm front to back, 320 mm end to end and 4 mm thick, 90 to 94 mm above the counter; under each end of it an acrylic end panel 80 mm by 4 mm and 90 mm tall standing on the counter (outer faces 320 mm apart, inner faces 312 mm apart); an acrylic front lip 312 mm long, 4 mm thick and 25 mm tall under the glass's front edge between the panels (65 to 90 mm up), its outer face flush with the glass's edge; and a hollow stainless end cap (0.5 mm sheet) 30 mm front to back, 24 mm wide and 25 mm tall on the glass at each end, centred front to back, its outer face flush with the shield's end (centres 296 mm apart). Overall 80 x 320 x 119 mm. Centred on the row, its panels stand 42 mm outside the row's ends and the lip's underside is 40 mm above the food, so it can pass over the pans without touching them. It starts standing on its panels on the staff side of the bar, square, front lip toward the customers, centred at x 17.0 cm, y +3.0 cm (x 13.0 to 21.0 cm, y -13.0 to +19.0 cm): pulled back for refilling, 30 mm toward the left end of the bar, its lip 49 mm behind the pans. Nothing else is on the table. In the simulator the acrylic is opaque (light blue-grey); a real trial uses clear acrylic.
scoring: The score is read from where the shield stands at the last step. 'Standing on its end panels': every corner of both panels' undersides within 3 mm of the counter top and the shield tilted 5 degrees or less (a panel on a pan, on the food or on the tray slide is not). 'Square': its lip faces the customers (+x) within 10 degrees seen from above (turned lip to the staff side is not square). 'Spans the row': its lip runs over both ends of the row of pans (y -11.4 and +11.4 cm). 'At rest': neither panel's foot moved more than 3 mm in the last 0.5 s. 'Overhang' is read with a tape at each end of the row (y +11.4 cm and y -11.4 cm), across the bar (along x), from the pans' customer-side edge (x 34.0 cm) to the lip's outer face at its mid-height, positive past the pans; both readings count. 'Centred': the shield's centre (midway between its end panels) within 15 mm of the row's centre along the bar (y 0). Score 0 unless the shield is standing on its end panels, square, spans the row and is at rest. Otherwise: 0.75 if both overhang readings are 45 to 75 mm (18 to 30 cm at full size); 0.25 if both are 25 to 90 mm but not both 45 to 75; 0 otherwise (under 25 mm the food is not covered from the customers' side; past 90 mm customers cannot reach the back of the pans; the tray slide stops the lip at 94 mm). Add 0.25 if it is centred, only when the overhang earned something. Band edges count as inside. Possible scores: 0; 0.25 (both readings 25 to 90 mm but not both 45 to 75, off centre); 0.5 (the same, centred); 0.75 (45 to 75 mm, off centre); 1.0 (45 to 75 mm at both ends, centred); every outcome maps to exactly one. Examples: the start (lip 130 mm short of the pans) 0; 60 mm and centred 1.0; 60 mm but 30 mm off centre 0.75; 35 mm or 85 mm centred 0.5, off centre 0.25; a panel resting on a pan, the shield held up off the counter, propped on the tray slide, turned more than 10 degrees, or slid along the bar past the end of the row 0. Turned a little, the two readings differ by about 4 mm per degree: turned 5 degrees about the 60 mm aim, they read about 50 and 70 mm, both still in the 45 to 75 band. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 3 s. In a real trial, a tape across the bar at each end of the row gives the two overhangs, a tape along the bar the centring, a 3 mm feeler gauge under each panel checks that it stands on the counter, and a top photo shows the angle.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction. The pans and food are fixed blocks (real pans sit in a cold well, the food heaped); touching them in transit is not scored. The shield is one rigid body of six boxes, its acrylic opaque in the simulator. Customers and sneezes are not simulated: the rule is the lip's measured overhang and the centring. The scorer sees only the shield, so a shield held still, standing in place, counts as set.
reset_notes: Stand the shield back on its end panels on the staff side, square, front lip toward the customers, centred at x 17.0 cm, y +3.0 cm (lip at x 21.0 cm). The pans, food and tray slide are fixed; in a real trial check that they have not moved (pans' customer-side edge on x 34.0 cm, row centred on y 0) and that the shield's caps and panels are tight. Nothing is consumed.
